needed_lemma: Mass-transport/unimodularity and the chapter-6 isoperimetric framework are the structural inputs; this skill does not contain a new sharp formula for the uncovered face sizes.
unproved_interface: Need derive the sharp vertex-isoperimetric constant for the unresolved regular/coregular parameter range; the MTP alone does not give the extremal finite sets.

needed_lemma: Distinguish FSF=WSF via harmonic Dirichlet functions from mutual singularity. PTN Corollary 10.19's singularity theorem requires every vertex to have an infinite orbit; do not weaken this to an infinite orbit somewhere. The 2026 swap-zero-one result makes stated swap-invariant events zero-one, but does not itself give a separating event for every distinct FSF/WSF pair. HL2003 is only the spherical-tree change-tolerance criterion and does not supply a separating event for arbitrary FSF/WSF laws.
unproved_interface: Need construct a measurable separating event for every nonidentical pair of FSF/WSF laws; separate zero-one properties under each measure are insufficient.

needed_lemma: Use the finite weighted UST distinct-edge determinant from BLPS’s unnumbered Transfer Current Theorem, eqs. Burton–Pemantle Theorem 1.1 (primary arXiv v1 read copy, physical PDF p. 4 / printed article p. 3) supplies the finite unweighted D-regular formula, while Lyons DPP/PTN supplies the weighted positive-contraction kernel. Keep fixed-coordinate negative association separate from random disjoint certificates.
unproved_interface: Need prove the BK disjoint-occurrence inequality for all increasing events under weighted UST, or find a counterexample; no cited source gives it, and transfer-current determinants/negative association alone do not prove it.

needed_lemma: Strassen gives an ordinary monotone coupling from FSF stochastic domination; test whether the joint law can be chosen invariant under the full automorphism group.
unproved_interface: Need an invariant coupling for arbitrary graphs beyond established sofic/amenable cases; a monotone coupling by itself has no invariance guarantee.

needed_lemma: Keep the target marginal equal to FSF while adding a jointly invariant random edge set of arbitrarily small individual edge probabilities and making the union connected.
unproved_interface: Need an FSF-specific invariant augmentation; LPS only proves FMSF plus independent Bernoulli(ε) edges is connected.

needed_lemma: Compare FSF connectivity for two Cayley graphs of the same group; separate this cross-graph invariant from tail or component-count zero-one laws on one graph.
unproved_interface: Need show FSF connectivity depends only on the group, or construct two generating sets with different connectivity; each forest’s component count being deterministic does not compare the two graphs.

unproved_interface: Need a one-endedness theorem for WMSF on nonunimodular transitive graphs or a counterexample; the cited MTP proof cannot be used unweighted.

unproved_interface: Need prove FMSF connected for every locally finite graph roughly isometric to a tree or produce an example; the cited “FMSF plus ε-percolation” theorem is weaker.

needed_lemma: Keep the established USF threshold d≤4 distinct from minimal-forest connectivity and compare the competing d<6/d<8 predictions. Alexander Theorem 2.6 is only a planar dual statement for an ambiguity-free lattice-like embedding; do not use it as a higher-dimensional minimal-forest connectivity theorem. Hutchcroft–Peres Theorem 1.1 has the direction high-dimension ubiquity implies low-dimension ubiquity, with a witness ubiquitous only in the lower dimension; Theorem 1.2 and the edge-coarsening/vertex-quotient criteria refine USF component geometry above dimension 8 but do not decide minimal-forest connectivity.
unproved_interface: Need determine exactly which dimensions give connected minimal spanning forest on Zd; uniform-spanning-forest phase results do not settle the minimal model. The HP2019COMP monotonicity, tree-ratio, coarsening, and quotient criteria concern USF, so the minimal-forest connectivity threshold remains unresolved by that source. When invoking Proposition 2.2, retain its simultaneous distinct-component event for the prescribed family (K_i); it is not an unconditional product estimate for arbitrary disjoint-set connections.

needed_lemma: Use the projection-determinantal representation of finite matroid basis laws (including the weighted UST after scaling incidence columns by sqrt(c(e))) and the rooted-forest/effective-resistance minor identities as exact finite-law context. Lyons's Proposition 4.9 is a higher-dimensional density statement only under an amenable group acting freely on X, cocompact k-skeleton, and b~_{k−1}(X)=0; it is not an additional BK estimate.
unproved_interface: Neither source controls the union over configuration-dependent disjoint witnesses. Fixed-coordinate negative association and determinant/rooted-forest identities do not prove the weighted UST BK inequality; A141 remains open.

needed_lemma: Theorem 1.1 gives a lattice special case: for d≥3, one WUSF sample is the everywhere-percolating base and an independently thinned second WUSF with arbitrarily small retention parameter yields a connected union; its added edge-set is translation-invariant and each edge probability is bounded by the thinning parameter.
unproved_interface: B064 asks for every Cayley graph. This paper covers only ℤ^d with d≥3 and does not settle other Cayley graphs or dimensions below 3.

unproved_interface: No step transfers these WUSF results to FMSF/WMSF; a minimal-forest end theorem under B067 assumptions remains to be established.

unproved_interface: The paper contains no minimal-spanning-forest connectivity conclusion, so it does not determine the C105 dimension threshold.

needed_lemma: For recurrent unimodular random rooted unweighted graphs, Theorem 1 gives equality of UST and graph end counts; Theorem 15 (PDF p. 18) gives the one-ended iff unique-harmonic-measure criterion without finite expected root degree. unproved_interface: The source does not treat minimal spanning forests or general weighted networks; no transfer to FMSF/WMSF end counts is proved.

needed_lemma: On a transient bounded-geometry planar triangulation with a suitable circle packing, Corollary 1.2 identifies harmonic Dirichlet functions with Douglas-integrable boundary data. A nonconstant Douglas-integrable trace therefore supplies a nonconstant finite-energy harmonic function in this restricted model; combined with the existing FSF=WSF iff HD=R criterion, it gives examples with FSF != WSF.
unproved_interface: This only supplies a witness in the stated planar packing class. It does not prove mutual singularity, address arbitrary infinite networks, or resolve A025; apply only after checking transience, the precise triangulation/double-packing, bounded geometry/codegree, and trace hypotheses.
